items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: Les McCann turned me on to Roberta Flack and I negotiated my first deal with royalties the same week I made the first Roberta Flack record which went on to sell four million pieces.

ctx.x: So you had a sort of a base salary and then —

I started at Atlantic for $250 a week. I took home $197. My records started coming out and I got pretty lucky pretty early. The stuff started selling so I renegotiated a contact about a year later. Because I actually had an offer from Blue Note at that time to go over there. And then I had a pretty good couple of years, another year as a salary, but Les McCann turned me on to Roberta Flack and I negotiated my first deal with royalties the same week I made the first Roberta Flack record which went on to sell four…
